import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 6

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/6](https://www.erdosproblems.com/6)
- [BFT15] Banks, William D. and Freiberg, Tristan and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Caroline L., Consecutive primes in tuples. Acta Arith. (2015), 261-266.
- [Ma15] Maynard, James, Small gaps between primes. Ann. of Math. (2) (2015), 383-413.
-/

namespace Erdos6

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$, where $d$
denotes the prime gap function.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6 :
    {n | primeGap n < primeGap (n + 1) ∧ primeGap (n + 1) < primeGap (n + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < \dots < d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6.variants.increasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) < primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry


/--
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n > d_{n+1} \dots > d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6.variants.decreasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) > primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos6

reformulations.difference: The conventional source indices are one-based, whereas Nat.nth and primeGap are zero-based.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: With p₁ = 2 and dₖ = pₖ₊₁ − pₖ, primeGap n = dₙ₊₁. The bijection n ↦ n+1 identifies the two witness sets, preserving both strict comparisons and infinitude. The complete equivalence is proved as main_index_iff in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: BFT15 Corollary 1 parametrizes runs by their number M ≥ 2 of gaps. Lean parametrizes by m adjacent comparisons, giving m+1 gaps, and permits m = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For m ≥ 1, set M = m+1; conversely, set m = M−1. The additional m = 0 case has no comparisons and its witness set is all of ℕ, so it adds no restriction. Adjacent strict inequalities characterize a strictly increasing run. Including the prime-index shift, the fully quantified equivalence is proved as increasing_full_iff.

reformulations.difference: As in the increasing variant, Lean counts comparisons rather than BFT15's gaps and includes the zero-comparison case.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Reindex M = m+1 for m ≥ 1, with the converse m = M−1. The m = 0 case is automatically true, and the reversed adjacent inequalities characterize a strictly decreasing run. The fully quantified equivalence, including one-based source indices, is proved as decreasing_full_iff.

sources_consulted: Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Consecutive primes in tuples, arXiv:1311.7003v3: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.7003 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1311.7003 — especially Corollary 1, its surrounding definitions and remarks, and its proof.

Maynard, Small gaps between primes, arXiv:1311.4600v3: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.4600 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1311.4600 — introductory results and the deduction of arbitrarily many primes in bounded intervals.
Public Erdős problem status database, entry 6: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/PrimeGap.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Nth.lean, Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean, Data/Nat/PrimeFin.lean, Data/Nat/Count.lean, Data/Finset/Range.lean, and Data/Finite/Defs.lean.
review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Their research solved tags agree with BFT15 and the public problem-status database. Nat.nth's finite-set default is unreachable for primes; Lean proofs confirm that every primeGap is positive and that natural subtraction agrees with integer subtraction. Boundary cases, monotonicity characterizations, and concrete increasing/decreasing triples were checked in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, which compiles without errors or warnings; the equivalence proofs do not depend on the sorry-backed problem theorems. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/6 returned a Cloudflare challenge, so its current webpage remarks could not be read. The mathematical checks instead used the cited primary papers, OEIS's explicitly linked problem-6 sequence, and the public status database. Detailed checklist notes are in /workspace/review/review-notes.md.
